concern_results.conclusion: No credible counterexample found. The notice claim uses an epoch of [st_dev, st_ino]. Appends keep both values, so the claim stays stable. A transcript replaced by rename gets a new inode and a fresh notice, as the test shows. Same-path inode reuse keeps suppression, which the plan documents. A missing, raising or syntactically invalid skill-loading.py falls into the broad except and prints the truthful notice every time; the minimal-runtime test covers all three. The actor digest covers session, agent_id and the realpath of transcript_path. agent_transcript_path is removed first, so the claim follows the transcript that is actually scanned. Positive evidence comes only from context_transcript, which returns empty skill lists unless the context is complete. Extraction reads requested_skills, which keeps the native Skill pending/failed contract and the complete Codex read. Handoff reads completed_skills, prior_handoff or contract visibility. Absent evidence re-raises into the notice path. It never becomes a block or a pass.

No bypass found. Markers only return None from stop_notice after the scan and evaluation have already run, so they cannot skip a check or grant verification. Forged session or actor values only change advisory deduplication. Before this diff, overflow already failed open with no block, so the extraction gate loses nothing. The only new quiet path requires a complete current context with an extraction request. stop_hook_active still bounds the handoff block. If the state directory is a symlink, O_NOFOLLOW makes the claim fail, the notice is still printed and nothing is written, as the test asserts. Oversized files are rejected on fstat size before parsing, and the unit test enforces this by patching json.loads to fail if called. Release publication and CI remain pending and are not claimed as passed.
